newsitem.title: USA: Key IMM currency futures finish lower.
newsitem.headline: Key IMM currency futures finish lower.

text.p: Key IMM currency futures finished lower as the dollar firmed in afternoon trading.
News that Russian President Boris Yeltsin had agreed to heart surgery later this month buoyed the dollar near midday and September yen futures extended losses.
September dipped as low as $0.009167, below support at $0.009170.
The dollar tested its topside in afternoon trading, but upside appeared limited as players remained wary ahead of Friday's U.S. August jobs report.
Jobs were forecast up 244,000 versus a 193,000 July gain.
The unemployment rate was seen at 5.3 percent, compared with 5.4 percent in the July report.
September sterling rallied early to the highest price all year on an upbeat Confederation of British Industry retail survey, but those gains faded later.
September Canadian dollars slid as bearish technicals mounted, posting an outside day with a lower close.
"They came through $0.7297 and then the focus was taken off the majors after Europe went home and there were some big players in Canada," an IMM trader said.
Overall, traders called key currencies' tone consolidative ahead of Friday's data.
September yen and Swiss francs posted inside days on daily bar charts, a sign of a pause in the market. September marks remained in the middle of this week's range.

In view of recent signs of strength in the U.S. economy, traders were focusing on U.S. debt futures. A strong jobs report Friday was seen cementing the opinion that policy makers will tighten rates at their September 24 meeting.

Dallas Federal Reserve President Robert McTeer said on Thursday the U.S. economy was running hot with no sign of a slowdown yet. He added that price indicators he watches showed little troublesome inflation yet.
Fed Governor Janet Yellen said the U.S. economy was operating with a small margin of economic slack.

September yen closed down $0.000039 at $0.009171, marks lost $0.0022 to $0.6736, Swiss francs fell $0.0008 to $0.8289, sterling fell $0.0006 to $1.5662, Canadian dollar slipped $0.0018 to $0.7228, Aussie dollar rallied $0.0027 to $0.7941, and Mexican peso fell $0.000275 to $0.130600. --Derivatives Desk 312-408-8750 E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
